description: “I’m Dhruvansh from KG2D! For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, I made The Musical Earth to show how weather changes in summer, winter, rainy and spring seasons.”
summary: For the NASA Space Apps Challenge (The Earth Information Jukebox), I made a video called The Musical Earth. In it, I explain four seasons: summer, winter, rainy and spring. For each one, I show my own drawing and dress up for that weather. I wear a cap and sunglasses for summer, a warm jacket for winter, carry an umbrella in the rain and fly a kite in spring. My video helps young children learn about Earth’s weather in a fun way.
details:
What does it do / how does it work?
My video teaches the different weather conditions on Earth. For each season, I show a picture, my drawing, and myself dressed for that weather, so children can see and remember it.

What benefits does it have?
It helps little children learn the seasons and how to dress and stay safe in each kind of weather.

What is the intended impact?
I want children to notice the weather around them and learn about our Earth, just like NASA scientists do.

What tools did you use?
I used a phone or tablet camera to record myself and a video editing app to add pictures, titles, stickers and effects. I also used my own drawings and props: a cap, sunglasses, a water bottle, a jacket, an umbrella and a kite.

How is it creative?
I acted out every season myself, made my own drawings, and presented it like a real NASA scientist.

What factors did I consider?

  • Seasons: I chose four seasons that children know.
  • Clothes and props: I picked the right ones for each kind of weather.
  • Easy to follow: Pictures and big titles help young children understand.
  • Clear speaking: Everyone can follow along.
